subject: anatomy
title: Epithelial Classifications, Cilia and Cell Junctions

steps.tx: Epithelial tissues are categorized by cell layer stratification and apical cellular geometry. An epithelium consisting of a single layer of flattened, scale-like cells with flattened nuclei is a **simple squamous epithelium**. Providing a minimal physical barrier that maximizes passive diffusion, it lines vascular lumens as endothelium, lines body cavities as mesothelium, and forms pulmonary alveoli.
steps.say: Epithelia are classified by layer depth and surface cell geometry. An epithelium made of a single layer of flattened cells with compressed nuclei is simple squamous epithelium. Minimizing diffusion distance, it lines blood vessels as endothelium and covers serous membranes as mesothelium.

steps.tx: A single layer of polygonal cells with equal height and width featuring central spherical nuclei represents a **simple cuboidal epithelium**. Adapted for active secretion and absorption, it lines the proximal and distal convoluted tubules of the kidney, lines the thyroid follicles, blankets the surface of the ovary, and forms the secretory ducts of salivary glands.
steps.say: A single sheet of polygonal cells with matching height and width and central round nuclei constitutes simple cuboidal epithelium. Specializing in active transport and secretion, it lines renal tubules, thyroid follicles, and salivary ducts.

left.title: Simple Squamous
points: Single layer of thin plate-like cells

steps.tx: Where tall cellular machinery is required for heavy synthetic and absorptive demands, **simple columnar epithelium** features tall rectangular cells with vertically oriented oval nuclei located near the basement membrane. Nonciliated columnar epithelium with surface microvilli lines the gastrointestinal tract from the stomach to the rectum, while ciliated columnar epithelium lines the fallopian tubes and uterus.
steps.say: When high metabolic capacity is required, simple columnar epithelium provides tall rectangular cells with basal oval nuclei. Lining the digestive tract with absorptive microvilli, it also populates the fallopian tubes with motile cilia to propel ova.

vis.alt: Epithelial classes: columnar, stratified squamous, and transitional
vis.caption: Comparative histology of columnar, stratified, and urothelial tissues. [Credit: StewardMD]

steps.tx: Appearing multi-layered because cell nuclei lie at varying depths, **pseudostratified ciliated columnar** epithelium is a single layer of cells where every cell contacts the underlying basement membrane, but only tall cells reach the luminal surface. Interspersed with mucus-secreting goblet cells, it lines the trachea, main bronchi, and nasal cavity as the classic respiratory epithelium.
steps.say: Appearing stratified because nuclei sit at staggered heights, pseudostratified ciliated columnar epithelium is a single layer where every cell touches the basement membrane. Interspersed with goblet cells, it lines the airway as respiratory epithelium.

steps.tx: Where tissues endure mechanical abrasion, stratified squamous epithelium features multiple layers whose superficial cells flatten. In **keratinised stratified squamous** epithelium, superficial dead cells lose their nuclei and pack with tough insoluble keratin, building the protective epidermis of the skin. Nonkeratinised stratified squamous epithelium retains living superficial nuclei, lining wet surfaces like the oral cavity and esophagus.
steps.say: Where physical abrasion occurs, stratified squamous epithelium provides multi-layered shielding. Keratinised stratified squamous epithelium sheds surface nuclei and packs with keratin to form skin epidermis, while nonkeratinised epithelium lines moist cavities like the mouth and esophagus.

points: Anucleate surface squames filled with keratin

right.title: Nonkeratinised Stratified Squamous
points: Resists mechanical abrasion in wet cavities

steps.tx: Specialized to withstand severe stretching and cytotoxic urine toxicity, **transitional epithelium**, or urothelium, lines the renal calyces, ureters, urinary bladder, and proximal urethra. Characterized by rounded, umbrella-shaped dome cells on the surface that flatten during bladder distension, the apical plasma membrane features rigid uroplakin plaques that form an impermeable barrier.
steps.say: Specialized to endure stretching and acidic urine, transitional epithelium or urothelium lines the urinary tract. Large umbrella dome cells flatten when the bladder fills, while apical uroplakin plaques form an impermeable barrier against toxic urine solutes.

nodes.label: Empty Bladder: 5-6 Layers with Umbrella Domes

steps.tx: All epithelia are supported by an acellular sheet called the **basement membrane**, separating epithelium from underlying lamina propria connective tissue. Comprising a basal lamina synthesized by epithelial cells (type IV collagen, laminin, entactin) and a reticular lamina synthesized by fibroblasts (type III collagen), it anchors cells, guides polarity, and acts as a selective filtration barrier.
steps.say: Epithelia rest upon an acellular basement membrane that separates them from connective tissue. Composed of a basal lamina rich in type four collagen and laminin plus a reticular lamina of type three collagen, it maintains polarity and serves as a filtration gate.

steps.tx: Lateral epithelial cell junctions form a junctional complex coordinating adhesion and permeability. The most apical band is the **tight junction** (zonula occludens), sealing intercellular clefts via claudin and occludin proteins. Below it lie zonula adherens (cadherin anchors), desmosomes (spot welds providing tensile resistance), and gap junctions (connexin channels permitting direct electrical and metabolic coupling).
steps.say: Epithelial cell junctions form an adhesive complex along lateral membranes. The apical tight junction seals intercellular spaces via claudins. Beneath it lie zonula adherens, robust desmosomes resisting shear stress, and gap junctions that allow direct ion flow.
